title: Start here
body:
Explore the available result tabs. Each view has its own filters, source details and plot controls.
Ask Module guide to open a view or change its settings. Use Apply on a proposed configuration and Undo to restore the previous settings.

title: Genome · Choose tracks
body:
In Genome Browser → Tracks, choose cell types and signal or peak tracks, then Apply tracks. refGene and Ruler stay visible as references.
ATAC signal shows continuous chromatin accessibility; peaks show called intervals. The default comparison includes up to six cell types, prioritizing the current selection. Default comparison restores those tracks; Select all includes all twelve cell types.
Try: “Compare alpha and beta signal tracks at compact height.” Follow with “Also include ductal” to extend the comparison.

title: Genome · Region, zoom & height
body:
Enter a GRCh38 interval such as chr7:117480025-117668665 and choose View. Coordinates are zero-based, half-open. Drag to pan; the horizontal zoom buttons change the genomic span. Reset returns to the starting region.
Track height offers Fit panel, Compact (80 px), Medium (160 px) and Large (260 px). More tools opens the genome browser’s additional controls. Fullscreen gives tracks more space; Download exports SVG.
You can also ask the guide to locate a gene, Ensembl ID or rsID. Variant navigation includes 500 bp on each side of the source interval.

title: scBrowser · Gene, highlight & subset
body:
Cell map displays all 448,935 cells from the PanKbase scRNA-seq v3.4 atlas. Enter a gene and choose View. Highlight selects a cell type; Selected toggles between that cell type and the full atlas.
Gray marks cells with no detected expression; blue shows increasing log-normalized expression. By cell type displays expression distributions. Source contains the atlas identifiers and methods.
Use the plot controls to zoom, fit, show cell details, download or enter fullscreen.

title: DE · Volcano & thresholds
body:
Choose a cell type and comparison in Dataset. Volcano plots log₂ fold change against −log₁₀ adjusted P.
Open Highlight and thresholds to change the absolute fold-change and adjusted-P cutoffs or highlight a gene. Red and blue mark positive and negative changes passing both cutoffs; orange marks the highlighted gene. Defaults are |log₂ FC| > 1.5 and adjusted P < 0.05.
Gene table lets you find, sort and download genes from the selected comparison.

title: DE · Heatmap and sample labels
body:
Heatmap shows the source-selected genes and samples for the current comparison. Rows are genes; columns retain the source sample order.
Colors show per-gene z scores from blue (−3) through white (0) to red (+3). Gray marks missing values. Hover for gene, sample and value.
Download exports the heatmap with sample labels. Source links to the original comparison.

title: Functional · Native response curves
body:
Response shows insulin or glucagon secretion normalized per IEQ or by hormone content. The figure includes stimulus windows, individual donor traces and the cohort mean.
Ask Module guide to filter by donor metadata or explicit donor IDs. For example: “Show functional responses for female donors with T1D.” Apply updates the cohort; Undo restores it.
Source lists the active filters, all donor IDs contributing to the mean, and the first 24 donors drawn as individual traces. Metadata filters combine with AND; an explicit ID list selects those donors directly.

title: PCA · Samples, coloring & PCs
body:
PCA map plots pseudobulk samples using any two of ten principal components. Cell type chooses the dataset; Color by chooses a sample attribute. Plot settings contains the X/Y axes and hover label.
Contributions lists the top ten genes for a selected PC. Percentages are squared source loadings normalized over all genes in that component. You can download the coordinates, contributions table or contribution plot.
Try: “Plot PC2 against PC3 and color by diabetes status.”

title: Knowledge Graph · Explore
body:
Knowledge Graph displays the returned entities and relationships. Select an entity or relationship to inspect its details. Use the toolbar to search, zoom, fit the graph, show hover information, download or reset the view.
The legend identifies entity and relationship types. Fullscreen expands the current graph; Escape returns to the result page.

title: Troubleshooting
body:
For a loading error, choose Retry in the affected view. Check Source for the selected dataset and version. Empty results may require a different gene, comparison or interval.
Escape exits fullscreen. Large track collections scroll vertically; heatmaps and expression distributions can scroll horizontally.
If guide chat is unavailable, the manual and visualization controls remain available. Start a New chat to clear the conversation.

title: Biological entities · Identity and coordinates
body:
Ask about a gene symbol, Ensembl ID, rsID, pathway or ontology term to see its identifier, annotation and source.
Genome placements include the assembly and zero-based, half-open interval. A unique GRCh38 placement can be opened in Genome Browser. If several records match, use a stable ID to select one.
Follow-up questions can refer to the most recently mentioned entity. Source references and versions are available with each lookup.

title: QTL · Credible sets and Manhattan plots
body:
Choose a QTL Source, enter a gene or complete credible-set ID in Gene / set, then choose View and select a Credible set. Clear the gene to browse all sets with Previous and Next.
Sources are pancreatic eQTL (PKBDS6689QROA), islet eQTL (PKBDS8062GYOQ), pancreatic sQTL (PKBDS2105PCON) and islet exon QTL (PKBDS9837ORWK). A set is identified by its source dataset and complete credible-set ID.
Manhattan plot shows −log₁₀(P), PIP and LBF with LD R² colors. SNPs are equally spaced in source order. The dashed line marks the first maximum-PIP SNP. Source provides the lead SNP and original credible-set table.
